# Edward Shen

> Case studies, essays and notes on Go backends, distributed scheduling, data platforms, and the systems around them.

These articles describe project decisions, production observations, and implementation limits. Proposed changes are identified in the articles.

## Author

- [About Edward Shen](https://edwardshen125.github.io/about/): Career background and systems owned.

## Case Study

- [Cutting Firestore Reads 58% by Moving a Scan Off the Request Path](https://edwardshen125.github.io/posts/cutting-firestore-reads-by-moving-a-scan-off-the-request-path/): A Firestore fallback query ran on every task creation: 347,901 executions and 31.6M read operations in 22 hours for 0.011 documents per run. A rate-limited Redis queue cut both by 58%.
- [Migrating a Billion Elasticsearch Documents Without Stopping Writes](https://edwardshen125.github.io/posts/migrating-a-billion-elasticsearch-documents-without-stopping-writes/): Migrating ~1B documents to a new Elasticsearch index without downtime — the mode switch, the resumable reindex runner, and the write-path decisions.
- [Designing a Predicate-Driven Audience Pipeline for Lifecycle Email](https://edwardshen125.github.io/posts/building-a-predicate-driven-audience-pipeline-for-lifecycle-email/): How reusable predicates, AST compilation, and layered TiDB data let lifecycle campaigns combine user traits, events, and expiring assets into email audiences.
- [Building a Real-Time Data Platform With TiDB CDC and Flink](https://edwardshen125.github.io/posts/building-a-real-time-data-platform-with-tidb-cdc-and-flink/): How a four-engineer backend team built a TiCDC, Kafka, and Flink data platform on TiDB for second-level analytics, reconciliation, and QueryHub dashboards.
- [Scaling Four Engineers to Eighteen Go Services With Generated Contracts](https://edwardshen125.github.io/posts/scaling-four-engineers-to-eighteen-go-services-with-generated-contracts/): How four Go engineers used a shared API DSL, code generation, and platform defaults to deliver eighteen production services while controlling contract drift.
- [Building a Production Go Scheduler for 200K+ Delayed Jobs per Second](https://edwardshen125.github.io/posts/building-a-production-go-scheduler-for-200k-delayed-jobs-per-second/): How a Go scheduling center used TiDB, etcd, and Pulsar to publish more than 200K delayed jobs per second, and how production incidents reshaped its isolation model.
- [Debugging a Sporadic Go OOM in a Recursive JSON Encode Path](https://edwardshen125.github.io/posts/debugging-a-sporadic-go-oom-in-a-recursive-json-encode-path/): A Go service hit its 8 GB Pod limit when a recursive event type entered jsoniter's lazy encoder compilation path. Bisection isolated it; moving only that publish path to sonic stopped the incident.
- [One Queue for Every State Change: Fixing Silent Over-Assignment in a Live QR Code System](https://edwardshen125.github.io/posts/one-queue-for-every-state-change-fixing-silent-over-assignment-in-a-live-qr-code-system/): A live QR code system kept sending customers to offline or over-quota salespeople. One Kafka queue, keyed per QR code, serialized every update to WeCom's routing config.
- [Running a Million-DAU Casual Game on Go: Rooms as the Concurrency Boundary](https://edwardshen125.github.io/posts/running-a-million-dau-casual-game-on-go-rooms-as-the-concurrency-boundary/): Go room-server architecture for a casual game with over one million DAU: serial ECS ticks, room-level concurrency, and map-to-array optimization.
